goal: Root-cause why identical repeated runs produce wildly different physics results
allowed_changes: (any file, if a concrete bug is found elsewhere -- keep changes minimal
notes: Honest inconclusive result, not a false 'fixed'. Confirmed: (1) the variance is real and substantial (not a fluke of one bad run), (2) it is NOT solely explained by the controller-spawn race (already fixed in CTRL-002, still present after), (3) it is NOT cleanly explained-or-fixed by either real_time_factor or use_sim_time changes -- both introduced their own new failure modes instead. Remaining candidate explanations, untested: genuine chaotic sensitivity to sub-millisecond timing in a nonlinear coupled system near a stability boundary; Gazebo/DART physics solver non-determinism unrelated to ROS-side timing. Recommend: either accept single-run PASS/FAIL as inherently noisy for large-disturbance scenarios and require multiple repeated runs before trusting a result (statistical acceptance rather than single-shot), or invest further dedicated time specifically in Gazebo/DART determinism research before trusting any single verification run in Phase 5+.
